newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian minister cleared in corruption case.
newsitem.headline: Italian minister cleared in corruption case.

text.p: A court cleared Transport Minister Claudo Burlando of complicity in fraud and abuse of office on Monday in a case linked to a construction project in the northwest city of Genoa, where he had served as mayor.
Examining judge Carlo Beconi dismissed the case against Burlando and threw out a charge of abuse of office against Vittorio Grattarola, a former councillor in the port city.
Both defendants belong to the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), the biggest force in the Italian centre-left government which took office last May.
Burlando was briefly arrested while mayor of Genoa in May 1993 in the case that came to court on Monday.
Prosecutors had alleged that a contract the city awarded to a construction company to build an underpass in 1992 had been inflated beyond its real worth.
They had asked the court to find Burlando guilty and sentence him to 14 months in jail.

The ex-communist PDS has been largely immune to the graft scandals that felled Italy's old political class when magistrates exposed entrenched corruption in public life in 1992. Building projects were a favoured conduit for kickbacks.
